column1: # Rules for check_style.py. Six tab-separated fields:
#   id   severity   scope   flags   regex   message
# severity: ERROR = the thesis has none of these; a new one is a defect.
#           WARN  = sometimes legitimate; read the hit, then fix it or accept it in baseline.tsv.
# scope:    all | abstract | front | body | sections | prose | notpolicy | nomodelapp | generated  (see SCOPES in check_style.py)
# If the regex has a group, the hit is reported at group 1.
# To add a term the thesis has settled on: add its drift forms here and its definition to terms.md.
# --- punctuation and devices the voice never uses ---------------------------------------------

column6: No em dashes. Use a full stop, a comma or "and".
No dash between words. An en dash joins number ranges only (1--30).
Two semicolons in one sentence. Split it.
No rhetorical questions. A question mark belongs only in a quoted research question.
No footnotes. Put it in the text or delete it (Cochrane).
Italics only to define a term at first use.
No contractions.
Write it out, or drop it.
One direction is enough (Cochrane).

column6: AI or inflated vocabulary. Use the plain word.
No adjectives about the work or its results (Cochrane). Give the number.
Intensifier or filler adverb. Give the number or cut the word.
Hedge. Scope a claim with "in the model" and a limit stated once, not with modal verbs.
might and "could" are rare here. "may" is kept for external or legal facts; model results are stated flat.

column6: Vague quantity. Give the tabulated number; "about" is the only approximator.

column6: Wordy phrase. Use "to", "because", "for" or "on".
Use the short word (use, start, show, need, after, before, while, among, on, through).
Cochrane: strike "I leave x for future research". The conclusion says what better data "would show".

column5: \b(this|these|which|the (result|finding|analysis)s?) (underlines?|underscores?|highlights?|emphasi[sz]es|illustrates?|reinforces?|speaks to|points to the (importance|need)|demonstrates? the (importance|need|value))\b|\bthe importance of\b|\b(taken together|all in all|in sum|on balance|the (key )?takeaway)\b
column6: No closing moral. End the paragraph on its last fact.
The thesis says "sensitivity" and gives the numbers. "Robust" survives only in table labels.
Never call the work illustrative.
The author is "we" and "our" (decided 2026-11-16; do not reopen). Never "I".
State the model as fact ("The household asks"). Keep "is an assumption" for a value no source gives.
Passive hiding who acts. Use "we" or a concrete subject ("We pair differences by seed").
No "one can see", no "the reader", no "this thesis aims to". Say what the thesis does and finds.
in which refers to a model; "where" refers to a place (Cochrane).
The convention is "detectable" (beyond two standard errors, Section 3.1). Never "significant".
A null is "not detectable", reported with its estimate and standard error.
No p-values, t-statistics or stars. Estimate, one standard error, and "detectable".
Differences in rates are "points" in the text and "pp" in tables. "Percentage point" appears once in the abstract and once where Section 3.1 defines the convention.
Levels are written with \% attached to the number.
pp is for table headers. In sentences write "points".

column5: \b(caus(e|es|ed|ing|al|ally)|prov(e|es|ed|ing)|confirm(s|ed|ing)?|establish(es|ed|ing)?|identif(y|ies|ied) the (mechanism|effect|cause)|drives?|driven by|leads? to|results? in|due to|explains?|the reason (for|why))\b
column6: Check the claim. The experiments show which assumptions an effect depends on; they do not identify mechanisms. Preferred verbs: raises, lowers, depends on, runs through, follows from the rules, accounts for.
Results hold in the model for two years and are not forecasts. Check the scope of the sentence.

column5: \b(in (reality|practice|the real world)|South African households (do|are|will|would|default)|policymakers? should|regulators? should|we recommend|should be (introduced|adopted|implemented|required|mandated))\b
column6: The thesis makes no recommendation and no claim about actual households. "Whether screening leaves households better off is open."

column1: # --- terminology: the canonical term is in terms.md ---------------------------------------------------

column6: Modelled units are "households". "Agent" belongs to "agent-based model", the data-to-agent tables and Appendices D to G.
household for the model. These words only for a cited source's own population (and "consumer credit profiles", "BNPL users" in a source).
In the model a BNPL seller is a "platform" and its contract an "agreement". "Provider" is for real firms and sources.
agreement, "instalment", "pay-in-four".
the traditional lender, then "the lender"; "traditional debt". "Banked" is the eligibility flag, not the lender.
facility was removed on 2026-11-16. Write "traditional debt or any BNPL agreement". Kept only inside the NCR category "credit-facility accounts".
The time unit is the "tick" (14 days), from Section 2 on. Before that write days or "two years".
arrears for unpaid instalments, "past due" for the age of one. Not overdue, delinquent or late.
The default trigger is "an instalment more than 90 days past due". Four older "behind" uses are in the baseline; do not add more.
shortfall is the defined term (Section 2). "Short of food and rent" is the state; "short from the start" is the group.
committed expenditure (food and rent). "Living costs" appears only in the phrase about what the platforms' screen compares.

column5: \b(the (very |extremely )?poor(est)? households|very poor households|households in (deficit|hardship|poverty)|income[- ]poor|cash[- ]poor|destitute|households that cannot (afford|cover|pay)|structurally (short|insolvent|in deficit)|deficit households|underwater households|reported income|survey income|stated income|declared income)\b
column6: The group is "households short from the start" (3.6%, Section 3.5): "surveyed income does not cover food and rent". Income is "surveyed", never reported or stated.

column5: \b(population default|default rates?|rate of default|defaults? rates?|share (of households )?in default|default share|default incidence|probability of default|default risk)\b
column6: Two measures are defined (Section 3.1): "default during the run" and "default including the starting stock". Name one of them; "default" alone means the first.

column5: \b(treatment effects?|impact of BNPL|BNPL impact|BNPL'?s (impact|effect)|causal effect|average effect|mean effect|ATE|marginal effect|headline (effect|number|result|figure))\b
column6: the BNPL effect or "the effect": the paired difference in default during the run between the BNPL arm and the baseline.
scenario is reserved for the Section 5 arms. Elsewhere: arm, run, sweep, switch, lever.

One configuration is an "arm"; one execution is a "run"; repeated runs are "replicates" on "seeds". Baseline = BNPL off. Benchmark = BNPL on, no regulation. Control = beta 0 or gamma 0. "Sensitivity", not "robustness", in headings and prose.

column5: \b(benchmark (without|with no) BNPL|baseline with BNPL|BNPL baseline|base ?case|base ?line scenario|status quo|reference scenario|default (settings?|configuration|parameteri[sz]ation))\b
column6: Baseline = BNPL off. Benchmark = BNPL on at the reference values with no regulation. Do not swap them.
In prose write "without BNPL" and "enabling BNPL". "No BNPL" and "BNPL off" are table labels.
The model switch is "bureau visibility". "Reporting arrangements" names the real-world change. Do not say "reporting raises default".
the Regulation 23A test, then "the lender's test"; the platforms apply a "light screen"; the switch is "mandatory screening", then "screening". A new screen needs its own fixed name in terms.md.
The arm is "the wage-income screen" (Section 4.1, tab:effect-split), always in full. It checks that surveyed income from employment or self-employment is above zero; it is not an affordability test.
The design is "the redrawn population"; each replicate has its own "population draw". "Resampled population" is the fixed 5{,}000 of Section 3.2.
platform cap = the lever on platforms owed. "limit" = the platform limit lambda. Other caps keep their full names: order cap, fee cap, shortfall cap, Regulation 23A payment cap.
Two "switches" (bureau visibility, mandatory screening) and two "levers" (cooling-off window, platform cap). Not interventions, instruments or policies.
peer influence. beta = 0 is "without peer influence". ("Peer adoption" survives only inside RQ2, which is frozen.)
The two uses are a "want-driven purchase" and borrowing "against a shortfall" (the "shortfall path").
the shortfall path. "Routing" already names the order in which a household tries platforms.
stacking: owing two or more platforms at once. Shares are of "ever-holders".
For model shares write "ever-holders" (held a BNPL balance at some tick) or "holders" (hold one now). "Users" is for cited sources.
credit-active (owing any traditional or BNPL balance or arrears, Section 2). "Indebted" names a different set in Appendix D.
starting stock, "starting profile", "starting arrears".
Parameter classes are fixed: Observed, Constructed, Imported, Derived, Fitted, Assumed, Swept (register: sourced, derived, fitted, assumed). "Fitted" is only payment friction and arrears persistence.
Validation words are fixed: "by construction", "checks consistency only", "no independent check", "weak evidence", "supports orders of magnitude only". The fitted profile cannot validate the model.
Top-level units are "Section~\ref{...}". "Chapter" never appears in the text.
the main research question, then RQ1, RQ2, RQ3. The RQ wording is frozen: do not reword or propose rewording.

column5: \b(our model|the simulation(?! (variance|stream))|the simulator|the ABM|the framework|our framework|the proposed model|the present (study|model|thesis))\b
column6: the model. "In the model" is the scope marker.
British spelling throughout (behaviour, modelling, labour, -ise, instalment).
Thousands are written 5{,}000 so LaTeX does not add a space.
Words for one to nine, digits for 10 and above (except at the start of a sentence).
Words for one to nine ("four platforms", "seven ticks", "two years").
References are "Section~\ref{...}", capitalised, with a tie. No \cref, no abbreviations.
An effect is "$X \pm Y$ points". The unit follows the first value in a sentence only.
Acronyms come from \ac{...}; never type the expansion and brackets by hand.
Spell out authors' names. "et al." has one full stop.
LaTeX quotes: ``like this''.
